behaviours.title: Opening a new account starts it at a balance of 0 with no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 0 and entries('A') is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: the account starts with a non-zero balance or an opening entry is recorded
contrary_alternatives: opening an account records an 'open' entry in its history
opening is refused because nothing has been deposited

behaviours.title: Re-opening an existing account keeps its balance and history
behaviours.given: account 'A' has received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: balance('A') stays 100 and entries('A') still holds the single deposit of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the account is reset to a balance of 0 with no entries
contrary_alternatives: open throws an error because the account already exists

behaviours.title: An account never opened reports a balance of 0 and no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'X' has never been opened or used
behaviours.then: balance is 0 and entries is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: reading the balance of an unknown account fails with an error or returns undefined
contrary_alternatives: reading the balance returns undefined
reading an unknown account throws 'unknown account'

behaviours.title: A deposit into an unopened account opens it and credits it
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'A' was never opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 100 and entries('A') is [{ txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }]
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected because the account does not exist and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' is open with balance 0
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero deposit is accepted and recorded as a deposit entry of 0
contrary_alternatives: the zero deposit is silently accepted as a no-op returning ok

behaviours.title: A negative deposit is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative deposit is accepted and the balance becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the amount is taken as its absolute value and the balance becomes 150

behaviours.title: A deposit of NaN is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' is open with balance 0
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted and the balance becomes NaN
contrary_alternatives: the deposit throws an error

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId reports success but credits nothing
behaviours.given: account 'A' received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: another deposit of 100 with txnId 't1' is made
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 100 and there is still only 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the duplicate is credited again and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the duplicate is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: A deposit reusing a txnId already used by another account is ignored
behaviours.given: account 'A' received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: 50 is deposited into account 'B' with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but balance('B') is 0 and entries('B') is empty
behaviours.contrary_then: txnIds are tracked per account, so 'B' is credited and its balance becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: An invalid amount is rejected even when the txnId was already used
behaviours.given: account 'A' received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: a deposit of 0 with txnId 't1' is made
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } (the amount is checked before the duplicate check)
behaviours.contrary_then: the duplicate txnId is recognised first and the result is { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the result is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to cents, with a half cent rounding up
behaviours.given: account 'A' is open with balance 0
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 0.13 and the entry amount is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: half a cent rounds to even (or is truncated) and the balance is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is kept unrounded and the balance is 0.125
the deposit is rejected because it has more than 2 decimals

behaviours.title: Sub-cent fractions below a half cent are rounded down
behaviours.given: account 'A' is open with balance 0
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 10 and the entry amount is 10
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is kept unrounded and the balance is 10.004
contrary_alternatives: the amount is rounded up to 10.01

behaviours.title: A deposit that rounds to 0 cents is accepted and recorded as an entry of 0
behaviours.given: account 'A' is open with balance 0
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 0 and an entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 0 } is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with reason 'invalid-amount' because it rounds to 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but no entry is recorded

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero withdrawal is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: a withdrawal entry of 0 is recorded

behaviours.title: A negative withdrawal is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative withdrawal is applied and the balance becomes 120
contrary_alternatives: the absolute value is withdrawn and the balance becomes 80

behaviours.title: Withdrawing more than the balance is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, the balance stays 100 and no withdrawal entry is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -50
contrary_alternatives: the available 100 is withdrawn and the balance becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance is allowed and leaves 0
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 0 and a withdrawal entry of 100 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds and the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: a minimum balance must remain, so the withdrawal is rejected

behaviours.title: Withdrawing from an unopened account is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'Z' was never opened
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('Z') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -10

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not consume its txnId, so it can be retried
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and withdrawal 'w1' of 150 was rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.when: 100 more is deposited (txnId 't2') and withdrawal 'w1' of 150 is retried
behaviours.then: the retry returns { ok: true } and the balance becomes 50
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as a duplicate: it returns ok but the balance stays 200
contrary_alternatives: the retry is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same txnId reports success but debits nothing
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and withdrawal 'w1' of 30 succeeded (balance 70)
behaviours.when: a withdrawal of 30 with txnId 'w1' is made again
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 70
behaviours.contrary_then: the duplicate is debited again and the balance becomes 40
contrary_alternatives: the duplicate is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and the balance stays 70

behaviours.title: A withdrawal reusing a deposit's txnId is silently ignored
behaviours.given: account 'A' received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: txnIds are tracked per operation type, so the withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes 60
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 is allowed
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and nothing withdrawn yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the limit is lower (e.g. 1000) and the withdrawal is rejected

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 exceeds the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and nothing withdrawn yet
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: only 5000 is paid out and the balance becomes 5000

behaviours.title: The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and withdrawal 'w1' of 3000 succeeded
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 7000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit applies per withdrawal, so it is accepted and the balance becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: only 2000 is paid out, reaching exactly 5000 for the day

behaviours.title: Cumulative withdrawals reaching exactly 5000 are allowed
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and withdrawal 'w1' of 3000 succeeded
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 7000
contrary_alternatives: reaching the limit exactly is treated as exceeding it

behaviours.title: The daily limit is tracked separately for each account
behaviours.given: accounts 'A' and 'B' each have a balance of 10000 and 'A' has withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('B') becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is shared across the ledger, so 'B' is rejected with reason 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the limit is per customer and 'B' is refused

behaviours.title: A withdrawal rejected by the daily limit does not use up any of the limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and withdrawal 'w1' of 6000 was rejected as daily-limit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the rejected 6000 counted toward the limit, so this is rejected as daily-limit
contrary_alternatives: the account is blocked for the day after a limit breach

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported ahead of the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the daily limit is checked first and the reason is 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: both reasons are reported together

behaviours.title: Withdrawal amounts are rounded to cents before the limit check
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and nothing withdrawn yet
behaviours.then: it is treated as 5000: the result is { ok: true }, the balance becomes 5000 and the entry amount is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the unrounded 5000.004 exceeds the limit and the withdrawal is rejected as daily-limit
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted but 5000.004 is debited

behaviours.title: A transfer of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and 'B' is open
behaviours.when: 0 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balances stay 100 and 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero transfer is accepted with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: transfer entries of 0 are recorded on both accounts

behaviours.title: A negative transfer is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and 'B' has a balance of 50
behaviours.when: -30 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balances stay 100 and 50
behaviours.contrary_then: money moves backwards: 'A' becomes 130 and 'B' becomes 20
contrary_alternatives: the absolute value 30 is transferred from 'A' to 'B'

behaviours.title: Transferring more than the source balance is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and 'B' is open with 0
behaviours.when: 150 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, 'A' stays 100 and 'B' stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer goes through: 'A' becomes -50 and 'B' becomes 150
contrary_alternatives: the available 100 is transferred and 'A' becomes 0

behaviours.title: Transferring exactly the whole balance is allowed and records both sides
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and 'B' is open with 0
behaviours.when: 100 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, 'A' becomes 0, 'B' becomes 100, 'A' gets a 'transfer-out' entry of 100 and 'B' a 'transfer-in' entry of 100, both with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected as insufficient-funds and balances stay 100 and 0
contrary_alternatives: only the source account records an entry

behaviours.title: Transfers are not subject to the 5000 daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and 'B' is open
behaviours.when: 6000 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, 'A' becomes 4000 and 'B' becomes 6000
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected with reason 'daily-limit' and balances stay 10000 and 0
contrary_alternatives: transfers have their own limit and this one is refused

behaviours.title: Transfers do not use up the daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 10000 and has transferred 5000 to 'B' (txnId 'x1')
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and 'A' becomes 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer counted toward the limit, so the withdrawal is rejected as daily-limit and 'A' stays 5000
contrary_alternatives: half the transfer counts toward the limit

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId reports success but moves nothing
behaviours.given: account 'A' had 100 and transfer 'x1' of 40 to 'B' succeeded ('A' 60, 'B' 40)
behaviours.when: transfer 'x1' of 40 from 'A' to 'B' is made again
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balances stay 60 and 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again: 'A' becomes 20 and 'B' becomes 80
contrary_alternatives: the duplicate is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A transfer to an unopened account opens it and credits it
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100 and 'C' was never opened
behaviours.when: 25 is transferred from 'A' to 'C' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, 'A' becomes 75 and 'C' becomes 25
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected because 'C' does not exist and 'A' stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'

behaviours.title: A transfer to the same account leaves the balance unchanged but records both entries
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 100
behaviours.when: 50 is transferred from 'A' to 'A' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance stays 100 and entries are deposit 100, transfer-out 50, transfer-in 50
behaviours.contrary_then: a transfer to the same account is rejected and no entries are added
contrary_alternatives: the balance drops to 50

behaviours.title: Transfer amounts are rounded to cents, half a cent rounding up
behaviours.given: account 'A' has a balance of 1 and 'B' is open
behaviours.when: 0.125 is transferred from 'A' to 'B' with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: 'B' receives 0.13 and both entries carry amount 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: half a cent rounds down and 'B' receives 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the unrounded 0.125 is moved

behaviours.title: entries returns a copy that callers cannot use to alter the history
behaviours.given: account 'A' received a deposit of 100 with txnId 't1'
behaviours.when: the list returned by entries('A') is emptied by the caller and entries('A') is read again
behaviours.then: the second read still holds 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the history is shared and the second read is empty
contrary_alternatives: entries returns a frozen list and emptying it throws
